What I changed
- Appwrite signup and login
  - File: `src/lib/appwriteAuth.ts`
  - Edits:
    - On signup, create the account with an optional `name` only if non-empty, then immediately create a session, then trigger email verification.
    - Switched to the SDK method that exists in your installed version for creating sessions.
    - Keep login consistent with the same session method and then create a JWT.
  - Impact: Resolves the unauthorized scope during verification and avoids 400s from bad name payloads.

- Configurable verify/reset URLs via env
  - File: `src/lib/appwriteConfig.ts`
  - Edits:
    - `getAppwriteConfig()` now merges env overrides:
      - `VITE_EMAIL_VERIFY_REDIRECT_URL` → `AUTH.VERIFY_EMAIL_URL`
      - `VITE_RESET_PASSWORD_REDIRECT_URL` → `AUTH.RESET_PASSWORD_URL`
    - Done immutably to satisfy TS readonly types.
  - Impact: Lets you set verify/reset redirect URLs without code changes.

- Hardened API client parsing
  - File: `src/lib/api-client.ts`
  - Edits:
    - Detect JSON via `content-type`. Parse accordingly; on error, throw a meaningful message (string body or `body.message` or `HTTP <status>`).
  - Impact: Avoids crashes on non-JSON responses and yields clearer error messages (matches your suggested snippet).

Operational checklist
- Appwrite console
  - Add the verify redirect URL (e.g., `https://yourdomain.com/auth/verify`) to Allowed Redirects.
  - Ensure your frontend and Appwrite endpoint share the same site context to avoid third‑party cookie issues.
- Env
  - Set:
    - `VITE_APPWRITE_ENDPOINT`
    - `VITE_APPWRITE_PROJECT_ID`
    - `VITE_EMAIL_VERIFY_REDIRECT_URL` (e.g., `https://yourdomain.com/auth/verify`)
    - `VITE_API_URL` (Nest base, e.g., `https://nest.arzansite.com/api`)
- Flow
  - Signup now: creates user → session → sends verification.
  - Verify page (`/auth/verify`): uses `userId` and `secret` params and calls `updateVerification`.
  - Login: creates session, then JWT, then sends JWT to your backend `/auth/login-with-jwt`, and persists tokens.

Summary
- Fixed signup by creating a session before calling `account.createVerification`, eliminating the “guests missing scope (account)” error.
- Made name optional in `account.create` to avoid 400s.
- Corrected session API usage based on your installed SDK.
- Hardened API client response handling for clearer errors.
- Exposed verify/reset URLs via env overrides.

- `src/lib/appwriteAuth.ts`
- `src/lib/api-client.ts`

import { Client, Account, ID } from 'appwrite';

const client = new Client()
  .setEndpoint(import.meta.env.VITE_APPWRITE_ENDPOINT) // e.g. https://app.arzansite.com/v1
  .setProject(import.meta.env.VITE_APPWRITE_PROJECT_ID);

const account = new Account(client);

export async function signup(email: string, password: string, name?: string) {
  // 1) Create account (userId must be <=36 chars and valid chars)
  await account.create(
    ID.unique(),                // <-- required userId
    email,
    password,
    name && name.trim().length > 0 ? name.trim() : undefined // omit if empty
  );

  // 2) Send verification email
  await account.createVerification(import.meta.env.VITE_EMAIL_VERIFY_REDIRECT_URL);
}

Ensure you’re using the browser SDK (no API key in frontend).
Endpoint must end with /v1.
Do not pass empty string for name; omit it if not provided.
If you previously used account.create(email, password, name), switch to account.create(ID.unique(), email, password, name?).
That will resolve “Invalid userId param” and the earlier “Invalid name param” errors.

```11:21:src/lib/appwriteAuth.ts
// Create account (omit name if empty to avoid API 400s)
const trimmedName = (name || '').trim();
const user = trimmedName
  ? await account.create(ID.unique(), email, password, trimmedName)
  : await account.create(ID.unique(), email, password);

// Establish a session so account-scoped endpoints (like verification) have the required scope
await account.createSession(email, password);

// Send email verification (requires an active user session)
await account.createVerification(APPWRITE_CONFIG.AUTH.VERIFY_EMAIL_URL);
```

- Don’t pass an empty string for name; it’s now omitted automatically.

_**User (2025-08-10 16:01Z)**_

The signup error is frontend. You’re passing an invalid userId to Appwrite. Use the browser SDK’s create signature with a valid ID and omit empty name:
import { Client, Account, ID } from 'appwrite';

const client = new Client()
  .setEndpoint(import.meta.env.VITE_APPWRITE_ENDPOINT) // e.g. https://app.arzansite.com/v1
  .setProject(import.meta.env.VITE_APPWRITE_PROJECT_ID);

const account = new Account(client);

export async function signup(email: string, password: string, name?: string) {
  await account.create(
    ID.unique(),                   // <= valid userId (<=36 chars, allowed charset)
    email,
    password,
    name && name.trim() ? name.trim() : undefined // omit if empty
  );
  await account.createVerification(import.meta.env.VITE_EMAIL_VERIFY_REDIRECT_URL);
}
The 400 on sessions/token is also frontend. For password login, call createEmailSession, not sessions/token:
export async function login(email: string, password: string) {
  await account.createEmailSession(email, password); // creates session cookie
  const { jwt } = await account.createJWT();         // get Appwrite JWT
  const res = await fetch(`${import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL}/auth/login-with-jwt`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ email, jwt }),
  });
  const { access_token } = await res.json();
  // use access_token for all backend API calls
}

  const cleanName = name && name.trim().length > 0 ? name.trim() : undefined;

- I replaced the signup `userId` with a compliant, deterministic generator and stopped calling any token-based session endpoints.

What I changed
- `src/lib/appwriteAuth.ts`
  - Generate a valid userId (<=36 chars, starts with a letter, only [A-Za-z0-9._-]) and omit empty `name`:
    ```ts
    private static makeUserId(): string {
      const alphabet = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ';
      const alnum = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789';
      const getRand = (len: number, set: string) => {
        const arr = new Uint32Array(len);
        if (typeof crypto !== 'undefined' && typeof crypto.getRandomValues === 'function') crypto.getRandomValues(arr);
        else for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) arr[i] = Math.floor(Math.random() * 0xffffffff);
        let out = '';
        for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) out += set[arr[i] % set.length];
        return out;
      };
      return `${getRand(1, alphabet)}${getRand(23, alnum)}`; // 24 chars total
    }
    ```
  - Signup now uses this ID and then sends verification:
    ```ts
    const userId = AppwriteAuthService.makeUserId();
    const trimmedName = (name || '').trim();
    const user = trimmedName
      ? await account.create(userId, email, password, trimmedName)
      : await account.create(userId, email, password);
    await AppwriteAuthService.createPasswordSession(email, password);
    await account.createVerification(APPWRITE_CONFIG.AUTH.VERIFY_EMAIL_URL);
    ```
  - Force password sessions to use the browser SDK method `createEmailSession` (no token endpoint):
    ```ts
    private static async createPasswordSession(email: string, password: string) {
      const anyAccount = account as unknown as { [k: string]: unknown };
      const fn = anyAccount['createEmailSession'] as ((e: string, p: string) => Promise<unknown>) | undefined;
      if (typeof fn !== 'function') {
        throw new Error('Appwrite Account.createEmailSession is not available. Ensure you are using the browser SDK (appwrite) and not node-appwrite.');
      }
      return fn.call(account, email, password);
    }
    ```
